title: Sunday school orchestra and the grandmother takes the horn back
summary: Willard gives his birth date and the 1921 dating; Davison knows church songs but misses Sundays and his grandmother confiscates the cornet until he begs it back.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let's just interject right here for the case of history that Bill was born on January 5, 1906 and the summer he is now talking about was the second summer; he was age 15 and it was in 1921. He first played Hamilton Lake when you were 14 years old.

Yeah. Well, anyway, I --- when I got back from the summer job and started to play in the Sunday school orchestra again, I was getting pretty big for that Sunday school orchestra and I thought I knew everything too. I knew--- I probably knew more church songs in the beginning - like - "Bring them in from the Fields of Sin" and "Onward Christian Soldiers" and all those songs; I knew all those songs.
You told me before you knew all those songs before you knew any real jazz music---

Oh, yes - I knew the melody and I could play the melody and that's all they needed in the Sunday school band. But, when I went back, I missed a Sunday or two and, uh, I didn't realize my grandmother meant what she said -- and one day she stormed in the library and said, I want that horn and I said - "why". She said - "Where were you last Sunday and the Sunday before" and something and I said, "Well, I wasn't feeling good". She said, "Well, I meant what I said - I want the horn." So, she took it. Oh, man, that almost killed me when she took that horn. So, uh, I went up to her house on my knees to get that horn back - promise her faithfully I'd go back and play in the Sunday school orchestra and, uh, -- so, you talk about how you get started. Now, these are weird ways to get started.
